races.name: Irish EBF Auction Series Fillies Maiden
Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap (Birdcatcher Series)

runners_data.name: Supreme Lord
runners_data.note: Well-treated prominent racer for Robson De Aguiar, has winning form at 6f on good, ran just nine days ago which is tight, but sim-going record of 4/4 is strong and Donagh O'Connor gives him a live chance from a handy pitch if he secures his spot.

runners_data.name: La Tache
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes over for G M Lyons on a filly who won at 5f on good but has been beaten in both 6f starts; the 43-day absence and a hood fitted for the first time are notable, and she needs to prove this trip suits before booking a place in the finish.

runners_data.name: Tradewinds
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type for Donnacha O'Brien — never won over six but has placed three times at the distance on good ground, wears a tongue-tie and hood, and Paddy Harnett's 3lb claim is a bonus for a horse who simply needs things to set up in front of her.

runners_data.name: I Ready
runners_data.note: Showed real grit to win at 6f on good last time and holds a prominent style that suits this trip; Reese Holohan's 7lb claim offsets some of the weight burden, though he ran in a cheekpiece previously and lacks that equipment today.

runners_data.name: Lars Soldier
runners_data.note: Consistent without winning over six furlongs, Wesley Joyce takes the ride for small-yard Mulvany and he ran just five days ago — freshness is a mild concern; best efforts have come in placed positions and he may find the prominent battle too hot on this occasion.

runners_data.name: Lady Patrona
runners_data.note: The only confirmed leader in the field, Shane Foley and Harrington have placed her perfectly off a 31-day break; won over 6f on good last time and her sim-going record of 4/4 underlines she handles these conditions — the unchallenged lead is the key asset.

runners_data.name: Shesthedevil
runners_data.note: Won a 6f good-ground maiden and prefers to come from off the pace for Patrick Magee; trainer has been quiet (0/5 over 14 days) but Chris Hayes is a strong booking, and if the prominent battle heats up this filly has the profile to arrive late.

runners_data.name: Howlin Wolf
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on good recently and wears a hood for the first time today, which Jack Davison runners have used with mixed effect; Declan McDonogh is a strong pilot for a hold-up horse whose last two form figures — 2 and 1 — show a horse in excellent nick at exactly this distance and going.

runners_data.name: Celestial Crown
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse for JP Murtagh whose form figures at six furlongs read 8-8 and who has no placed efforts in five career starts — mapped to midfield because hold-up positions are congested, which means she is unlikely to get any version of her preferred race; form figures give little encouragement regardless.

runners_data.name: Captain James Cook
runners_data.note: A natural prominent runner for Aidan O'Brien and Wayne Lordan, but his three career figures are 6-7-12 and he cannot be expected to secure a prominent spot in this competitive field — his redistribution to midfield reflects the crowded pace picture, and raw form is too weak to compensate.

races.paceDynamic: Lady Patrona is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with Shane Foley aboard for Harrington, she is expected to stride out from the gates and control the tempo on her own terms over Navan's flat six furlongs — a sustainable, uncontested lead rather than a scorched-earth gallop. Behind her, Supreme Lord, La Tache, I Ready, and Lars Soldier all want prominent positions, creating genuine congestion in the 2-3 wide berths available behind the leader, with traffic interference and early jostling a real risk from the off. Captain James Cook is a natural prominent type who is unlikely to secure that position in this field and has been mapped to midfield, while Celestial Crown is a genuine hold-up horse similarly displaced; neither can be trusted to run their true race in this shape. With one honest pace-setter dictating a controlled tempo and a cluttered prominent bunch likely to burn energy wrestling for position, this race shape favours hold-up types who can settle, travel smoothly through the field, and produce a sustained late run into the straight — Howlin Wolf, Shesthedevil, and Tradewinds are the natural profile beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lady Patrona Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Patrona breaks sharply and is allowed to bowl along uncontested at a fair but controlled gallop.
scenarios.body: She sets every fraction to suit herself, the prominent scrimmage behind her consumes energy early, and she is far enough clear to repel late challengers on a flat track where leaders are respected.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners burn each other off chasing Lady Patrona, leaving the hold-up brigade with a clear run off the turn.
scenarios.body: Howlin Wolf and Tradewinds, both proven on good ground at six furlongs, get cover through the race and produce their finishing kicks as the prominent horses stop in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent War Blows Up
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent horses — Supreme Lord, La Tache, I Ready, Lars Soldier — fight hard for position and push the pace beyond Lady Patrona's comfort zone.
scenarios.body: The tempo becomes genuinely hot and the race is set up for a closer who has travelled wide of the carnage; Tradewinds' consistent placed form at six furlongs on good ground makes her a natural beneficiary.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Drifter Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If Captain James Cook or Celestial Crown, both racing out of their natural roles and mapped to midfield, manage to find an unexpectedly clear passage and hit the line from off the pace.
scenarios.body: This scenario demands things to go wrong elsewhere and these runners to outperform their likely race positions — Captain James Cook's limited form figures make this low-probability, and Celestial Crown's poor placed record at six furlongs on good ground adds further doubt.

watchPoints.text: Lady Patrona — watch how cleanly she breaks; if anything blunders out of the gates and forces her wider or into a battle for the lead, the entire race shape unravels and the hold-up horses become the dominant profile.

Supreme Lord, La Tache, I Ready, and Lars Soldier — four horses fighting for two or three prominent positions means watch the first two furlongs for bumping, interference, and energy wasted; any horse forced wide or off the bridle early is compromised.

Howlin Wolf — the first-time hood is a variable to track; if it settles him into a rhythm and McDonogh gets him into a smooth position three wide off the turn, his recent form over this exact trip and going makes him the most dangerous late mover.

Captain James Cook — Wayne Lordan is capable of improvising, but if Cook fails to secure any natural rhythm and ends up flat-footed in midfield with cover in front, his three poor form figures suggest he has little left to offer from that position.

Tradewinds — the combination of tongue-tie, hood, and a 3lb claimer riding a horse trained to come from behind means watch where Harnett positions her early; if she is too far back or trapped on the inside rail around the two-furlong marker, her finishing kick will be wasted.

races.name: Navan Racing Festival Early Bird Tickets On Sale Now Handicap

runners_data.name: Agostino
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist 281 days off the track, trainer 0/2 in 14 days and form showing no win or place on similar Good ground (0W0P in 15 sim-going runs); needs a gap to materialise in a packed 19-runner field that makes his natural late style almost structurally impossible here.

runners_data.name: Irish Rumour
runners_data.note: Ran 14 days ago over 6-7f on Good, but this 5f trip is at the short end of her range; hold-up style with 5 placed runs from 13 on similar going shows consistency, but a congested rear in this field is a serious obstacle to finding clean air.

runners_data.name: Rosato
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Charles Weld with Shane Foley aboard; ran 7 days ago and has a strong record of placing (1W3P in 10 sim-going runs) with two second-place finishes over 6f Good — drops in distance to 5f here which is the one query, but natural position suits the race shape well.

runners_data.name: Surpass And Shine
runners_data.note: Hold-up style on a horse that has won twice on Good ground over 5f (2W4P in 12 sim-going runs), but the form string of 100-00 shows two recent blanks; 20 days off and the question is whether she has the early pace to get competitive from off the pace in a large, fast field.

runners_data.name: Asdana
runners_data.note: Visor-wearing hold-up runner for W McCreery, 90 days off the course; trainer is a strong 6/19 in 14 days suggesting yard is in form, but most recent runs have come on Soft/Heav and the switch to Good at 5f with a long absence is a significant combination of risks.

runners_data.name: Lethimfly
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride which is eye-catching, but the form figures of -20000 hide a horse that has run 18th and 16th recently; hold-up style over 5f on Good (1W4P in 12 sim-going runs) with trainer 1/11 in 14 days — the jockey upgrade is the only hook.

runners_data.name: Simmering Seas
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up/prominent type that has placed twice from 7 runs on similar going and has two second-place finishes in recent form; Ben Coen takes over after a 7-day turnaround and this 3-year-old looks the most credible of the horses mapped toward midfield, with the physical pace to get closer than its nominal position suggests.

runners_data.name: Steel Magnolia
runners_data.note: Visor-wearing prominent racer who WON 13 days ago over 5f Good for W McCreery (trainer 6/19 in 14 days with yard clearly firing); form of 434721 shows rapid improvement and the natural prominent position perfectly suits the dominant race shape — the most live contender from a profile standpoint.

runners_data.name: One Cool Bear
runners_data.note: True hold-up type mapped to midfield because the rear is structurally overcrowded; 85 days off and form of 244700 shows no win or place on Good ground, and the STYLE_FIT discount of 0.92 means the repositioning further undermines an already modest chance.

runners_data.name: Glen Breeze
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse that is realistically unable to get its preferred position with the field this congested; dropped from 6-8f to 5f sharply and most recent runs have been over longer trips — the winning run over 6f Good is the one positive but the trip and positional squeeze combine against it.

runners_data.name: Caffu Zafeen
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type whose recent form shows a ninth as best return in five runs on Good ground (0W2P, both places minor); forced toward midfield in a redistribution that does its chances no favours, and the raw form makes it very hard to make a case regardless of shape.

runners_data.name: Cleopatra Dream
runners_data.note: 239 days off the track for Diego Dias, with only three career runs and a noted tendency to fade in the finish; mapped to midfield from a true hold-up position, but sparse form, long absence and the fade flag make this a very difficult race to approach confidently.

runners_data.name: Monastere
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish tag is a key flag for a horse competing in a sprint that is decided in the final furlong; a notable win and place over 6f Good is on the profile but the step back to 5f and the redistribution away from its natural hold-up position leave Karl Thornton's runner facing an uphill task.

runners_data.name: Ballysax Lil' Mick
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the race and the architect of the entire pace map; OR of just 43 and form figures of 6-0605 show no recent win, but the uncontested lead at 5f Good is a genuine tactical asset — whether the eight-year-old has enough quality to capitalise on his own pace advantage is the central question.

runners_data.name: Step Back In Time
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent racer with an outstanding course-and-distance record (2W4P from 14 runs on similar going and 14/15 sim-going appearances); Gary Carroll takes over and the horse has placed third here over 5f Good recently, making it one of the best positional fits in the race.

runners_data.name: Kidd
runners_data.note: Only three career runs and all on Good ground (0W0P), with form figures of 780 giving little encouragement; fade flag plus redistribution out of natural hold-up position and a short form book make this a very speculative entry with John McConnell's yard running 3/30 in 14 days.

runners_data.name: The Love Machine
runners_data.note: True hold-up runner placed into midfield by redistribution; form of 000059 shows a fifth and ninth as career highlights, and a best run of 5th from 19 starts on similar going (1W1P) is hard to build a case on — the 31-day return and trainer 0/2 in 14 days add no encouragement.

runners_data.name: Jackandthefox
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with consistent placed form over 6-7f (0W2P in 8 sim-going runs) who drops to 5f here; Rory Cleary takes the ride for Miss Jennifer Anne Lynch and the recent form of -05455 shows a horse that finds a place without threatening — natural style suits the race shape but the trip may be too sharp.

runners_data.name: Lismacbryan
runners_data.note: Fade flag and hold-up style combine badly in a 5f sprint where the finish is everything; visor-wearing with a worst-of-field 19th on 5f Good last time, and the redistribution out of the hold-up zone means Siobhan Rutledge will be seeking a position this horse has historically struggled to find.

races.paceDynamic: Ballysax Lil' Mick is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field over 5f at Navan, and with no genuine rival to press him for the lead, he sets a controlled, uncontested pace from the front — a scenario that historically rewards horses who can sit just behind and pounce without burning energy fighting for position. Step Back In Time and Rosato are the likeliest horses to slot into prominent positions behind him, shaping the early order in the first two furlongs before the inevitable sprint to the line. The redistribution note is important here: One Cool Bear, Glen Breeze, Caffu Zafeen, Monastere, Cleopatra Dream, Kidd, The Love Machine, and Lismacbryan are all genuine hold-up horses crammed into a field where the rear will be extremely congested, meaning none of them can truly execute their natural closing run from an unchallenged back position. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit within two lengths of Ballysax Lil' Mick's controlled fractions and produce a straight sprint finish, while the overcrowded hold-up contingent face a structural disadvantage in finding clear daylight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prompt Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Ballysax Lil' Mick dictates a comfortable tempo unchallenged and prominent horses settle just behind without pressure.
scenarios.body: Ballysax Lil' Mick rolls along in front with Step Back In Time and Rosato tucked in behind, and the race becomes a sustained sprint from the 2f marker where the first two positions translate directly to winning positions; controlled fractions on Good ground at 5f at Navan suit horses who can travel strongly in the first half.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is just brisk enough to string the field and those poised in second or third rank quicken decisively in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Step Back In Time and Rosato sit perfectly placed within two lengths of the leader and hit the front before the hold-up horses have space to run through; this is the shape where a horse with a recent win or consistent placed form in similar company over 5f Good ground — like Steel Magnolia or Simmering Seas — translates position into victory.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Crowded Closers Break Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and a traffic-free gap opens for one of the redistrubuted hold-up types to surge late.
scenarios.body: This depends on genuine hold-up horses like Agostino or Irish Rumour finding an unlikely clear passage in a 19-runner field where the rear is structurally overcrowded; the STYLE_FIT discounts attached to the redistributed runners make this a low-probability shape, and Good ground on 5f at Navan rarely produces the dramatic late closers that would make it viable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Shock Result
scenarios.trigger: If Ballysax Lil' Mick goes too fast early and burns out, causing a scramble home where an outsider finds daylight from a wide draw.
scenarios.body: A breakneck early gallop would theoretically bring the field together late, but with no genuine challenger pressing Ballysax Lil' Mick for the lead this is an unlikely trigger; the main beneficiary in this unlikely shape would be a lightly-weighted horse stepping sharply in class like The Love Machine or Glen Breeze, neither of whom has the form profile to inspire confidence.

watchPoints.text: Steel Magnolia and Step Back In Time are the two horses whose natural prominent running styles fit this race shape best — watch if either drifts in-running to confirm they have secured the desired early position behind Ballysax Lil' Mick.

Ballysax Lil' Mick's early sections are critical: if he is pressed for the lead by any of the field's prominent types scrambling forward, the pace will quicken sharply and his chance of lasting home over 5f will shrink considerably.

The redistribution of eight hold-up horses into a congested rear creates a serious traffic-management risk in the final furlong — watch for interference among One Cool Bear, Glen Breeze, Caffu Zafeen and company as they simultaneously seek running room.

Asdana's trainer W McCreery is 6/19 in the last 14 days and also runs Steel Magnolia; it is worth noting whether yard intent is concentrated on one runner over the other, as both cannot represent the same tactical plan given their different running styles.

Colin Keane's booking on Lethimfly is a significant upgrade for a horse with moderate recent form — if Keane produces an unusually forward-positioned ride rather than the customary hold-up, the horse's chance would increase materially in this particular race shape.

races.name: Christmas Parties At Navan Racecourse On 6th & 13th December Handicap

runners_data.name: Erosandpsyche
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator (hg: tp) who sits naturally at the rear; has placed twice at 5f on Good including a runner-up recently, but the 0W in 6 similar-going runs is a red flag and Reese Holohan's 7lb claim must compensate for a horse that needs pace to be injected in front of it.

runners_data.name: Thunderbear
runners_data.note: 77 days off the track for Stephen Thorne is the dominant concern here; races from the rear (hg: tp), has a win at 6f on Good but only 1 win from 15 similar-going starts, and Jack Kearney's 3lb claim softens the burden — watch for fitness in the final furlong after the layoff.

runners_data.name: Amiata
runners_data.note: Four wins in similar going conditions and Colin Keane in the saddle represent genuine class at OR 88, the highest effective rating among the hold-up contingent; however, she is a true hold-up type crammed into a field of closers, meaning she is likely to race closer than ideal, and the style-fit tag tempers confidence despite strong form.

runners_data.name: Namiid
runners_data.note: Ben Coen rides a horse that prefers to race prominently (hg: p) and has made the frame in four of five starts at 5f on Good — the profile fits this race shape perfectly; OR 82 and JP Murtagh's yard in reasonable 14-day form, making this one of the more natural matches to the dominant scenario.

runners_data.name: Allsortz
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field and therefore the key pace-setter; Luke McAteer will be unopposed on the lead over 5f on Good ground, which gives Allsortz total control of tempo, though the recent form string (313074) and 0 wins in similar going underline that controlling the race is not the same as winning it.

runners_data.name: Moltophino
runners_data.note: Races prominently (hg: tb) for a trainer with 0 wins from 4 in 14 days and a recent run 14 days ago; the form string (-97992) is uninspiring but Chris Hayes takes over and the prominent style suits this shape — the issue is that every recent result at 6f on Good has been well beaten.

runners_data.name: Gotta Catch'em All
runners_data.note: Won twice in similar conditions and was placed in five of 15 similar-going starts, but ran only 3 days ago which raises recovery concerns; a natural hold-up type placed in midfield by redistribution, so racing closer than preferred, and the style-fit discount applies despite the respectable win record.

runners_data.name: Dandyville
runners_data.note: A bleak form profile (000-00 last five, 0W2P in 15 similar-going starts) for a trainer with 0 wins from 7 in 14 days; an 8-year-old natural hold-up type also running 3 days after last start, carrying the highest weight impost (119lbs) at OR 72 — the redistribution and form combine to make this a very difficult proposition.

races.paceDynamic: Allsortz is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pressing threat from another natural leader, should be able to bowl along at a controlled, honest pace over this 5f on Good ground at Navan. Namiid and Moltophino will push forward to claim prominent positions just off Allsortz, meaning the race will have a visible tempo without descending into a war — a measured but legitimate gallop that does not hollow out. The field carries significant hold-up inventory in Amiata, Gotta Catch'em All, and Dandyville, but none of these three are likely to get their preferred rails-scraping late position given how many genuine closers are competing for the same ground — Erosandpsyche and Thunderbear are the more natural rearward types who will actually race that way. This race shape firmly favours the prominent-to-lead profile: a controlled single-pace scenario over 5f on Good ground rewards horses who travel handy and do not need cover, while true closers face congestion at the rear and a pace that is unlikely to be severe enough to compensate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Allsortz Controls, Prominents Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Allsortz leads unchallenged at a fair clip and handy horses track smoothly to challenge in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Allsortz sets a sustainable tempo and the first wave of challengers — Namiid and Moltophino — press forward from a close position, with one of them pouncing as the leader ties up inside the final 100 yards; the prominent pitch is rewarded because the pace is never fierce enough to soften them up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Flood Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong early and creates a compressed, tiring finish that opens a late lane.
scenarios.body: Erosandpsyche or Thunderbear, the two authentic hold-up runners in this field, benefit if the front group over-commits and the final furlong becomes a cavalry charge; on Good ground over 5f this is possible but requires a pace uplift not currently in evidence.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Hold-Ups Outrun
scenarios.trigger: If Amiata, Gotta Catch'em All, or Dandyville manage to seize a closer-than-expected position and the pace is just strong enough to set them up.
scenarios.body: Amiata has the class (OR 88, Colin Keane, four wins in similar conditions) and if she travels smoothly just off the heels of the leaders rather than being anchored at the back, she could motor through; however, all three are racing out of role and the style-fit discount applies, making this a minority outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Muddle, No Clear Winner
scenarios.trigger: If crowding at the break or a slow early pace causes a bunched, tactical sprint where draws and stall exits dictate positions.
scenarios.body: A chaotic early furlong scrambles the expected shape, removing Allsortz's uncontested lead advantage and compressing all eight runners into a wall entering the final 2f; the outcome becomes lottery-like and any horse holding a favourable draw or quick break could prevail.

watchPoints.text: Allsortz must be tracked from the stalls — if anything challenges early for the lead and drags him into a faster-than-intended tempo, the whole prominent-dominated shape collapses and closer types benefit.

Amiata's redistribution is the key swing factor: if Colin Keane elects to ignore the hold-up pack and positions her prominently from the outset, her class at OR 88 makes her significantly more dangerous than her mapped position suggests.

Both Gotta Catch'em All and Dandyville ran just 3 days ago — watch for any market drift indicating trainer concern; quick turnarounds over 5f on Good ground can expose residual fatigue in the closing stages.

Thunderbear's 77-day absence is worth monitoring in the betting — if the market supports him despite the layoff, it may indicate a stable whisper about fitness, which would meaningfully elevate the hold-up scenario's probability.

Namiid's draw and early stride pattern should be watched; as the prominent horse most naturally suited to the dominant shape, any poor break or wide position could compromise what is otherwise the best-fitted profile in the race.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Return Of The Jumps At Navan Racecourse September 19th Handicap (Div I)

runners_data.name: Albatala
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old prominent racer with a recent win at 10f on Soft; Sam Coen (5) takes 5lbs off and this 10f Good trip suits, though the 55-day break and a history of big-field placings rather than victories are the main concerns.|

runners_data.name: Katherine
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up mare who has been racing regularly; Conor Lamon (10) riding, but her recent form — nothing placed closer than 4th in similar company — suggests she needs things to fall perfectly at the back of a 24-runner field.|

runners_data.name: Pallatine Hills
runners_data.note: Hold-up type trained by the Harty yard who has been running over sprint trips; this step up to 1m2f is a significant question mark for a four-year-old whose last five runs are all over shorter distances.|

runners_data.name: God Knows
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who won at 10f on Good but has been running over sprint trips of 7-8f in most recent outings; the drop back to a middle-distance trip needs to produce improvement that hasn't been evident lately.|

runners_data.name: Make The Tide
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who won over 8f on Good ground recently but will be shuffled forward into a midfield position by the sheer weight of closers in this field; W J Lee rides, having run just three days ago which merits monitoring.|

runners_data.name: Neon Eyes
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse with a second at 10f on Good and a fourth over this 1m2f trip; Gary Carroll is an asset and Gavin Cromwell's 73-day freshener could sharpen a three-year-old who clearly handles Good ground.|

runners_data.name: African Affair
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who fades in finishes and has been off 110 days; just three runs in the book, all on Good or Soft, and the fading tendency in a big field with traffic risks makes her chance slim.|

runners_data.name: Alto Sax
runners_data.note: Naturally races at the rear but will be pushed into a midfield berth by the volume of closers; placed four times in 15 Good-ground runs and has form over 12f, so the trip is not an issue — but racing out of role tempers expectations.|

runners_data.name: Jazz Forever
runners_data.note: Prominent type who tends to fade in finishes; has been running over longer trips of 13-16f and the drop back to 1m2f may help, but the fading tendency makes holding off closers in the straight difficult.|

runners_data.name: Mare Crisium
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner in this field, ridden by Shane Foley for K J Condon; has finished in the top six in all five Good-ground runs but lacks a win, making her vulnerable if prominent stalkers organise behind her.|

runners_data.name: Nephin Mountain
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who is a two-time winner on Good going including over 10f; Terry Casey (7) rides, and the three-year-old's recent Good-ground wins suggest genuine ability — gets weight off but needs a clear run.|

runners_data.name: Wipeawayyourtears
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a win over 12f on Good and placed twice in eight Good-ground runs; Jack Cleary (5) claims, ran just five days ago, and the blinkers are a notable factor for a three-year-old clearly in current form.|

runners_data.name: Calamint
runners_data.note: A horse that naturally wants to race at the rear but is pushed into a mapped midfield slot by the crowded hold-up contingent; placed three times in 15 Good-ground efforts over 10-16f, with Donagh O'Connor in the saddle.|

runners_data.name: Oh I Do Declare
runners_data.note: Fades in finishes and carries the longest absence in the field at 143 days; a three-year-old with limited form, all on Soft or Heavy, making this Good ground and big-field scenario a significant ask while being forced to race closer than natural.|

runners_data.name: Chloe's Boy
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up horse who has finished no closer than sixth in five Good-ground runs; fades late and being positioned closer to the pace than ideal by redistribution, with Siobhan Rutledge riding, makes this a tough ask.|

runners_data.name: Kingcharles
runners_data.note: Fading finisher with five straight Good-ground runs all resulting in placings of eighth or worse; Rory Cleary rides but the consistent pattern of weakening and being displaced from a natural hold-up role is a significant negative.|

runners_data.name: Churchill Gale
runners_data.note: Returning from 304 days off for Dermot McLoughlin; showed some ability in midfield positions over 10-11f on Good, but the length of absence and being forced off a natural hold-up style by the field's composition is a heavy price.|

runners_data.name: De Songbird
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has been running over sprint trips of 6-8f; the step up to 1m2f is untried for this hold-up type, and being pushed closer than natural by redistribution only adds to the task for Sadhbh Tormey (7).|

runners_data.name: Cause I Like You
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has been racing over 8f but has placed twice on Good ground; Wesley Joyce (3) claims, ran six days ago, and the stamina question over 1m2f remains open — natural style is rear but maps to midfield.|

runners_data.name: Miss Ivor
runners_data.note: Consistent in finishing mid-to-rear of the field on Good ground; Jimmy Dalton (7) up, fading tendency noted, and this three-year-old has been plying her trade over sprint trips — the 1m2f trip is a stamina extension.|

runners_data.name: Capall Cuain
runners_data.note: Unplaced in three runs on Good, all over sprint trips; Gavin Ryan rides this three-year-old who fades in finishes and has no form evidence to suggest she can handle this trip or field size.|

runners_data.name: Bang Po
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who fades in finishes and is returning from 11 days rest; five recent Good-ground runs all ended outside the top six, and running over 8f or 13f predominantly makes the 1m2f optimistic — Reserve jockey 1 listed.|

runners_data.name: Haeret In Pectore
runners_data.note: Five-year-old off 125 days for A J Martin, carrying a Reserve jockey booking; has only one placing on turf in recent runs and handles Good going in limited sample — the lengthy break and uncertain jockey situation are both concerns.|

runners_data.name: Giselles Defence
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up horse who won over 8f on Good ground and has placed twice in 15 Good-ground runs; Sean Davis sends her here on a three-day turnaround with a Reserve jockey booking, and being pushed closer than natural adds risk.|

races.paceDynamic: Mare Crisium is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 24-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace pressure — Shane Foley can dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m2f trip on Good ground. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up horses, many of whom are tagged as redistributed because the map cannot physically accommodate the volume of closers who would naturally race at the rear — Kingcharles, Oh I Do Declare, Make The Tide, Chloe's Boy and Churchill Gale are among those who will be forced further forward than ideal, compressing the midfield and creating traffic. Albatala and Jazz Forever are the main prominent types who will try to track Mare Crisium, but neither is likely to put her under serious pressure early, meaning the pace will be measured rather than searching. With a lone uncontested leader able to control fractions and the pack bunched behind, this race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently in the slipstream of Mare Crisium — particularly those who can quicken from a covered position into the straight without needing to weave through a compressed midfield.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Front Runs Free
scenarios.trigger: If Mare Crisium is allowed to dictate an uncontested, honest-but-not-brutal gallop and kicks clear in the straight before the midfield pack can organise.
scenarios.body: Mare Crisium sets her own rhythm with Foley nursing her into the straight, and the sheer volume of horses bunched behind creates traffic for closers, leaving the prominent stalkers best placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to stretch the field and the horses tracking Mare Crisium in the first three lengths have the class to overpower her in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Albatala or Nephin Mountain sits just off the leader and produces a sustained run from two furlongs out, while Mare Crisium's lack of a win suggests she will be caught once headed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Finisher Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly genuine, the field strings out, and one of the better-credentialled midfield horses finds a clear run down the straight.
scenarios.body: Neon Eyes or Wipeawayyourtears, both with genuine form at this trip, finds daylight late and picks off the tiring leaders — though the compressed, traffic-heavy nature of a 24-runner field makes a clean passage far from guaranteed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Mare Crisium goes far too fast for the conditions and ties up inside the final two furlongs, leaving a rare opportunity for a true closer to emerge from the pack.
scenarios.body: A horse like Nephin Mountain or Cause I Like You, with the stamina to sustain a run, benefits from a late collapse at the front — but with only one confirmed leader setting a controlled pace, this scenario requires an uncharacteristic misjudgement from Foley.

watchPoints.text: Mare Crisium (Foley) dictates fractions entirely unopposed — if she gets a soft lead and is allowed to coast through the early stages, the field will be chasing a horse who has controlled every parameter of the race.|

The 24-runner field contains at least eight genuine hold-up horses who will all be forced into the midfield pocket simultaneously — watch for severe traffic and crowding on the turn into the straight, particularly affecting Wipeawayyourtears, Neon Eyes and Nephin Mountain.|

Make The Tide and Alto Sax are natural closers being mapped to midfield by redistribution — both ran within the past nine days, and if either gets keen racing out of role earlier than preferred, it could compromise their finishing effort.|

Nephin Mountain is a two-time winner at 8-10f on Good ground — watch whether Terry Casey (7) elects to ride more prominently than the horse's style label suggests, which in this race shape could be a decisive tactical advantage.|
Wipeawayyourtears ran just five days ago and won over this exact trip (12f) on Good ground — monitor the market for any drift that might signal the quick turnaround has taken a toll before the off.|

races.name: Return Of The Jumps At Navan Racecourse September 19th Handicap (Div II)

runners_data.name: Nibras Rainbow
runners_data.note: The sole genuine front-runner in this race; recent form shows a win and a second, handles Good ground well across 10 runs, rides well at this trip, and the uncontested lead gives him every chance — discount slightly for the STYLE_FIT flag suggesting he may race out of natural role at this OR level.

runners_data.name: Miss Crinshawn
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare for Peter Fahey ridden by Ben Coen; only nine days since last run, handles Good ground, has a placed effort at 1m2f, but consistent hold-up style means she is a genuine rear-of-field type fighting for position in a very crowded back half of the field.

runners_data.name: Ballaghkeen
runners_data.note: Bolger three-year-old returning after 323 days off — that layoff is a major concern and form figures of 6-7-0-0 suggest limited ability even when fit; Good-ground record at shorter trips offers no confidence over 1m2f on this comeback.

runners_data.name: Keilah
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for McNiff who has shown a placed record in similar going but is stepping up from mainly 10f efforts; a fall in recent form (U in form string) adds an element of risk and 24 days since last run is no red flag, but the very crowded hold-up section makes positioning difficult.

runners_data.name: Millhone
runners_data.note: Charles Weld's three-year-old has four placed efforts from five recent runs all on Good ground at 11-14f, making this her optimal distance and going combination; a genuine hold-up runner who will face a large traffic challenge, but Rory Mulligan (5lb claimer) and consistent each-way form make her the standout finisher if the pace develops.

runners_data.name: Deuteronomy
runners_data.note: Fades in finishes according to form, and is a true hold-up runner pushed to midfield on the map by the crowd of rear-of-field types — racing out of role here with STYLE_FIT=0.90 and 42 days off; on Good ground over 10-12f he has placed once but the redistribution and fade flag reduce his claims materially.

runners_data.name: Strike De Vega
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type whose recent form figures of 0-6-0-0 offer nothing to work with; fades in finishes, was beaten wide in a 14f staying event, and 9 days since last run won't help if the horse hasn't shown improvement — a very short case.

runners_data.name: Queen Leila
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for Noel Kelly who has won on STA and placed on STA but has only two runs on Good, both showing limited form; stepping up dramatically in trip from 6-8f to 1m2f is a significant ask and she is likely to struggle with positioning in a field this large.

runners_data.name: Tickle The Cat
runners_data.note: Kevin Coleman's three-year-old fades in finishes and has posted 0-8-0-7 in recent runs — no evidence of competitiveness at this level; hold-up style and poor finishing record make her a very unlikely beneficiary of any race shape.

runners_data.name: Trishuli River
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up runner shuffled to midfield on the map because the back of the field is overcrowded — likely to find traffic a major issue in a 24-runner race; two placed efforts at 1m4f on STA are the form peaks and 47 days since last run is manageable, but STYLE_FIT=0.91 signals the mapped position flatters her tactical outlook.

runners_data.name: Captain Con
runners_data.note: Colin Keane picks up this three-year-old for Noel Meade after 63 days off; form of -0-0-6-7-0 is dire on Good ground and the fade-in-finish flag compounds the redistribution concern — the jockey quality is the sole positive note in a weak profile.

runners_data.name: Thegooseiscooked
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old for Gerard Keane who has consistent Good-ground experience (11 runs in similar going) and a placed record at this trip; the horse has historically been a hold-up type forced into an unnatural midfield slot by the crowded rear, and a STYLE_FIT of 0.91 tempers confidence, but course form and experience give him an outside chance if the race unravels.

runners_data.name: Morning Approach
runners_data.note: W McCreery's eight-year-old has a strong trainer 14-day record (6/19) which is the headline angle; however the fade-in-finish flag, a string of 11th, 11th, 14th finishes on Good ground, and the redistribution from true hold-up to midfield all point firmly against — trainer form is the only reason to look twice.

runners_data.name: Borora Aura
runners_data.note: Michael Mulvany's three-year-old is one of only three genuine prominent-style runners in the race, which is a major asset in a field dominated by hold-up types; headgear noted (t), 9 days since last run, and a second-place finish at 10f on Good ground mean this horse could sit just behind Nibras Rainbow and mount a serious late challenge.

runners_data.name: Emily's Boy
runners_data.note: Thomas Dowling's three-year-old returns after 147 days off with form figures of 0-9-0-0 in soft/heavy/sta ground — no Good-ground form to speak of; a genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield, the fade flag and the lengthy absence combine to make him among the least likely beneficiaries here.

runners_data.name: Wingit
runners_data.note: Patrick Magee's three-year-old has one second-place effort at 13f on Good and has shown ability at staying trips; fades in finish and is a true hold-up runner displaced to midfield, with headgear (t) and 21 days since last run both neutral factors — finishing record and redistribution lower the ceiling considerably.

runners_data.name: Arizona Star
runners_data.note: Michael Mulvany's three-year-old ran just six days ago and showed an 8th on Good ground; has one placed run at 10f on Good but fades in finishes and is a genuine hold-up runner moved to midfield by the crowded field — the very quick turnaround and fade flag are the dominant notes here.

runners_data.name: Due In June
runners_data.note: Ian Donoghue's three-year-old has six consecutive Good-ground runs all showing finishes of 6th-9th, making her one of the most consistent non-placers in the field; headgear (tp), 6 days since last run, and a true hold-up style pushed into a false midfield position all point to the same conclusion — not competitive.

runners_data.name: Connova
runners_data.note: Sheila Lavery's three-year-old has four consecutive placings at 10f on Good ground (4th, 3rd, 3rd, 4th) and is a hold-up type with legitimate each-way credentials if she can find room; a 24-day absence is fine, and the consistent finishing pattern in similar conditions makes her one of the more interesting of the redistributed midfield brigade.

runners_data.name: Cadreville
runners_data.note: Jarlath Fahey's three-year-old has been stepping up in trip progressively with a 3rd at 10f on Good being the form peak; 43 days since last run, headgear (p), and a true hold-up style mapped to midfield — consistent improvement with each run makes her a watch at big odds despite the positional disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Sunny Dude
runners_data.note: D Buckley's six-year-old runs mainly at 12-16f and has struggled badly on STA surfaces; form figures of 4-0-0-7-6 and a fade-in-finish note make him very unappealing at 1m2f on Good, and 61 days off with no jockey listed is a further red flag.

runners_data.name: Carrickfinn
runners_data.note: Shane Gallagher's seven-year-old returns after 125 days off with form on Soft and STA rather than Good ground; fades in finishes, no jockey listed, and no Good-ground form to speak of — the redistribution to midfield from a true hold-up style completes a difficult profile.

races.paceDynamic: Nibras Rainbow is the only confirmed front-runner in this 24-runner field and, with no genuine rival looking to press for the lead, he should coast along at a sustainable, controlled tempo from the front on Good ground over 1m2f at Navan. That uncontested lead means the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which historically suits horses who can travel prominently and pounce before the straight rather than deep closers relying on a true stamina test. Borora Aura and He Knows When are the two other prominent-style runners who can realistically sit just behind Nibras Rainbow and exploit that comfortable early pace, giving the front two or three a material positional advantage. The field is dramatically overloaded with hold-up types — Deuteronomy, Onyeisi, Captain Con, Trishuli River, Thegooseiscooked, Morning Approach and many others are genuine rear-of-field horses mapped to midfield purely because there is no room at the back — and the redistribution note confirms those horses are unlikely to get their natural position; this race shape strongly favours horses who can secure a prominent or front-rank position early and sustain it through a moderate gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nibras Rainbow Leads & Kicks
scenarios.trigger: If Nibras Rainbow dictates an uncontested, moderate tempo and quickens from the front in the straight without being reeled in.
scenarios.body: Nibras Rainbow's confirmed front-running role on Good ground at 1m2f, his recent form figures of 1 and 2, and his Going OK tag make him ideally placed to control fractions and sprint clear before the pack organises; his OR=58 is competitive and the absence of any challenger for the lead amplifies this advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Nibras Rainbow's lead is pegged back approaching the straight and the two genuine prominent types immediately behind him overhaul him in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Borora Aura and He Knows When are the two horses capable of sitting just off the slow fractions without burning energy, leaving them poised to strike as Nibras Rainbow reaches the limit of his stamina; at 1m2f on Good ground with no pace pressure, this positional duet is the most logical threat to the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Runner Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally stronger than expected and creates enough of a gap in the straight for one genuine hold-up finisher to thread through beaten horses.
scenarios.body: Millhone is the standout hold-up runner with four consecutive second-place finishes and a consistent Good-ground record, meaning she has the finishing mechanics to exploit any late opening; Miss Crinshawn also has placed form at 1m2f on Good and is ridden by Ben Coen who can position her optimally, making her the secondary beneficiary if closers do get in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In Big Field
scenarios.trigger: If the large 24-runner field produces traffic incidents, early scrimmaging and an unusually fast pace that scrambles the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: In a field this size even a moderate early surge can cause interference that disrupts the established order, potentially bringing a midfield horse who avoids trouble into contention; Thegooseiscooked has the course form and consistent Good-ground record (11/15 sim-going) to benefit from chaos, though his redistributed hold-up profile and age of nine mean this remains a low-probability outcome.

races.name: Lynn Lodge Stud Maiden

runners_data.name: Ben Lomond
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse across his entire career profile (including a third over 16f on Good), he has been pushed into a midfield mapping by field congestion — his chance is best framed through trainer Kyne's modest 14-day strike rate and a form string of 9-0 suggesting he has found his level; discount him unless something dramatic opens up late.

runners_data.name: Deetee
runners_data.note: Off 706 days since last run but showed a placed effort on debut at 9f on Good for Lupini — the layoff is a massive unknown, but the prominent style and any residual freshness could make him dangerous if he has trained on; zero wins from two runs, and the trainer's 14-day record (0/6) offers little confidence.

runners_data.name: Highlander Addict
runners_data.note: Has won once from seven runs (17f, Good) suggesting he needs an extreme test of stamina that 1m2f may not fully provide — Robyn Donaghue-Leahy takes the 7lb claim and his hold-up style is genuine, but he is placed to midfield by field size and this trip looks short of his ideal.

runners_data.name: If Not For Grace
runners_data.note: Tagged as a hold-up horse who fades in the finish, and three runs all resulted in double-digit finishes on Good ground — James Ryan can do little with a horse who has shown zero ability to pick up, and there is nothing in the profile to suggest 1m2f on this surface unlocks improvement.

runners_data.name: It's Good To Talk
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse whose natural rear position has been compressed by the crowded field — his best effort was a second over 16f at Heafy, making this shorter trip a concern, and the fade-in-finish flag compounds the doubt; Emmet Mullins sends him in on a 38-day break but the 000 form string speaks for itself.

runners_data.name: Medadthebookie
runners_data.note: Six runs without a win or a place finish on Good ground, consistently finishing in the rear half of the field, and a fade-in-finish flag underlines the pattern — Edward Buckley's 14-day record (0/5) adds no encouragement, and 1m2f looks no more forgiving than the distances he has already failed at.

runners_data.name: Scorcher's Son
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's in-form yard (11/67) saddles this four-year-old who was seventh on debut over 8f on Good — 1m2f is a step up in trip that could suit a hold-up profile, but one run is slim evidence and Declan McDonogh on board is the strongest positive angle.

runners_data.name: Nugentstown Sue
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up mare who fades in the finish and has not won from eight recorded runs — a 5-day turnaround is noteworthy and Nicola Burns takes the 5lb claim, but double-digit finishes are the norm and nothing in the profile suggests she can reverse that trend in a 23-runner field.

runners_data.name: Four Ball
runners_data.note: A three-year-old whose hold-up tendencies cannot be easily accommodated in this field size — mapped to midfield as a result, Gavin Ryan rides for in-form Ciaran Murphy (2/16 in 14 days), but two runs of 10th and 6th on Good give little to work with; the style-fit tag applies real pressure on his chance.

runners_data.name: Giordano
runners_data.note: Has faded in both runs at 10f on Good, and his natural hold-up style is further compromised by being pushed into midfield by field congestion — Rory Cleary rides for Kilmartin, who has a thin recent strike rate, and a form string of 9-0 offers nothing to build a case around.

runners_data.name: Gulf Beat
runners_data.note: Unraced and completely unknown stylistically — trained by the powerful Joseph Patrick O'Brien operation (11/67 in 14 days), this three-year-old is one of the blank-slate wildcards that could emerge from anywhere; J M Sheridan in the saddle is worth noting but the absence of any form makes this purely speculative.

runners_data.name: Handani
runners_data.note: Consistent placed performer (2-2-3 from three runs, all on Good ground) who races prominently and has shown he can travel and quicken over 8-10f — the step to 1m2f for D K Weld and Chris Hayes is the main question, but the prominent style ideally suits the pace this race will be run at and he is a logical beneficiary of Camelot Queen's uncontested lead.

runners_data.name: Heriot's Hope
runners_data.note: Unraced for A Oliver, a yard that has been quiet (0/12 in 14 days) — W J Lee takes the ride but there is zero form to interpret, and the UNKNOWN style and going tags mean this runner is a pure leap of faith in any scenario analysis.

runners_data.name: Legato
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Michael Mulvany (1/12 over 14 days) with Wesley Joyce claiming 3lb — the style and going are UNKNOWN and this is a maiden over 1m2f against 22 rivals; nothing to anchor a view, though the claim is a small positive if the horse is forward enough to use it.

runners_data.name: Metallic
runners_data.note: Two runs for O'Brien — 12th and 8th on Good over 12f — and a fade-in-finish flag identifies a recurring issue; the hold-up style is genuine but his natural position has been compressed by the large field, and there is nothing in the form to suggest he can turn around these performances at the same trip.

runners_data.name: Michinaga
runners_data.note: Has some form at 12f on Good (6th) and at 9f (9th) — Charles Weld's yard is quiet recently (0/7 in 14 days) and the lightly-raced UNKNOWN tag means the style read is uncertain; Rory Mulligan takes a 5lb claim and there may be more improvement in him than two runs suggest, though he needs to show it.

runners_data.name: Mississippi Shine
runners_data.note: Unraced for G M Lyons, one of the sharpest yards on the Irish Flat (5/27 in 14 days), with Colin Keane — Ireland's champion jockey — engaged; the UNKNOWN style and going tags mean he is speculative, but the stable/jockey combination demands respect in a wide-open maiden and he is the headline unknown in SCENARIO_D.

runners_data.name: Royal Bones
runners_data.note: Placed on debut (2nd over 8f on Good) and then dropped back to 6th over 10f — the step to 1m2f for Mrs John Harrington (3/32) and Shane Foley could be the making of him if stamina is the key, and a prominent profile suits the pace dynamic well; he is a leading candidate in SCENARIO_B.

runners_data.name: Steppinoncats
runners_data.note: One run — 12th over 7f at Sligo on Standard — and a fade-in-finish flag for Rory Devine (0/6 in 14 days); Luke McAteer rides and there is nothing in the single run to support any confidence over 1m2f on Good, making this one of the more speculative entries in the field.

runners_data.name: Twin Nation
runners_data.note: Unraced for Noel Meade (0/24 in 14 days — a striking blank) and ridden by Seamie Heffernan, whose presence on a debut type always merits attention — the UNKNOWN tags make this a pure unknown, but Heffernan does not partner maidens at random and this is a name to note if the betting moves.

runners_data.name: Vico Road
runners_data.note: Unraced for John Joseph Murphy (0/8 in 14 days) with Gary Carroll in the saddle — UNKNOWN across style and going, and the trainer's quiet recent form reduces the ante-post excitement; Carroll is a capable judge and if the horse is ready, the trip could suit a strong stayer's profile.

runners_data.name: Camelot Queen
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who holds all the positional cards — Lordan can dictate an uncontested pace from flag to finish, and her form shows the ability to hold a place (3rd twice on Good) without burning out; the OR of 72 is modest but irrelevant if she controls the tempo over rivals who cannot easily overhaul a horse on a Good surface at 1m

races.paceDynamic: Camelot Queen is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 23-runner maiden, and with no genuine rival to press her for the lead, Wayne Lordan can dictate an uncontested, controllable gallop from the front over 1m2f on Good turf at Navan. The pace will be honest but measured — a lone leader over this trip on Good ground rarely collapses, and Camelot Queen's form shows she stays in contention without burning herself out early. The redistributed hold-up horses — Giordano, Four Ball, Ben Lomond, and Sakoku — are genuine closers by style but cannot all find their natural rear position in a 23-runner field, meaning several will race closer to the pace than intended, muddling the midfield picture rather than creating a clean late challenge. This shape strongly favours horses who can sit prominently behind the leader and time a smooth run through, with prominent racers like Handani and Royal Bones ideally placed to travel on the pace without burning energy — late-closing hold-up types face a compromised scenario with a sustainable gallop and no wall of pace to reel in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Camelot Queen Controls Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Camelot Queen is allowed to stride clear and set a measured, unchallenged gallop that the field cannot close down in the straight.
scenarios.body: Lordan takes advantage of the lone-leader scenario to dictate every increment of pace, injecting just enough tempo to stretch the field without burning her reserves, and the steady Good-ground gallop becomes impossible to overturn for hold-up horses with no winning burst of pace on offer at the end; prominent horses close enough to her run into minor money but lack the gear to pass her.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Camelot Queen's control is genuine but one of the prominent-style horses travelling smoothly just behind produces a sharper turn of foot in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Handani has shown a consistent pattern of finishing in the frame by travelling prominently and picking up on Good ground, and Royal Bones — second on debut — has the profile to sit close to a manageable pace and deliver at the business end of a well-run 1m2f.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closer Lands Running
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is slightly stronger than expected and creates enough pace to set up a genuine late challenge from the midfield cluster.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on one of the displaced closers — most likely Sakoku, who showed a clear step forward to second over 13f on Good at Leopardstown — finding cleaner passage than the large-field congestion typically allows and picking up strongly through beaten horses; the style-fit discount on these horses (all STYLE_FIT-tagged) makes this less reliable, but Sakoku's best run profile makes him the standout candidate if it materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debut/Lightly-Raced Type Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unraced or lightly-raced three-year-olds — Mississippi Shine, Twin Nation, Heriot's Hope, Vico Road or Gulf Beat — is significantly ahead of their current assessments and produces a performance that a form-based map cannot anticipate.
scenarios.body: With five runners carrying UNKNOWN going/style tags from stables of the calibre of Lyons, Meade, O'Brien and Murphy, a dark-horse debut winner is a live possibility in a wide-open maiden where the form book is genuinely limited; Colin Keane on Mississippi Shine (Lyons) and Seamie Heffernan on Twin Nation (Meade) are the most notable jockey-trainer combinations to respect in this scenario.
